egypt.finding: The pound's fall is mostly local: the dollar is up 8% against it in a month, 0.8% against majors. The EGX30 rose 0.6% to 49,596 as Banque du Caire's offering was executed.

close.title: Thursday's close
close.note: A dash is a figure not yet confirmed by two sources this morning.

top.headline: The pound's slide is local; the EGX waits on the central bank
top.body: The dollar is up 8% against the pound in a month but only 0.8% against major currencies, so about 90% of the move comes from Egypt, not the dollar. The EGX30 rose 0.6% to 49,596 on Thursday, but the session's flows were swamped by the execution of Banque du Caire's offering, so they say little about who is backing the market ahead of the central bank's decision.
top.view: Neutral on the EGX30 into Sunday. A weakening pound and a pending rate decision argue for waiting; Sunday's first session after the decision is the real signal.
top.moves: Dollar earners (Orascom, Elsewedy) gain from a weaker pound; developers (Talaat Moustafa, Palm Hills) suffer if rates rise to defend it.
top.wrong: Sunday's turnover tops its 90-day average with foreigners net buyers outside the offering, or the pound steadies.
top.notice: Reports of a 100 bp rate hike after Thursday's close come from one source and could not be confirmed. The view above does not rely on them.

helped.name: Banks: CIB, EFG Holding
helped.why: High rates protect lending margins and T-bill income. CIB rose 0.5% on Thursday and is 17% up this year.

helped.name: Dollar earners: Orascom, Elsewedy
helped.why: A weaker pound lifts the pound value of dollar revenue; the dollar is up 8% against the pound in a month.

helped.name: Ports: Alexandria Containers
helped.why: Up 1.5% on Thursday and 29% this year; momentum, not news, so the call is weak.

hurt.name: Developers: Talaat Moustafa, Palm Hills
hurt.why: Higher rates raise buyers' financing costs; Talaat Moustafa is down 8% in a month and flat this year.

hurt.name: Telecom Egypt
hurt.why: Down 1.7% on Thursday and 11% in a month after an 83% run this year; profit-taking, no company news found.

hurt.name: Fertilisers: Abu Qir
hurt.why: Down 3.5%, the worst of your Egyptian names on Thursday; no company news found, likely profit-taking after a 73% run this year.

egypt.stocksNote: Worst on Thursday: Abu Qir −3.5%, no company news found. Best: Alexandria Containers +1.5%.

week.event: EGX reopens after the central bank
week.why: The first chance to price the rate decision; watch banks and developers in the first hour.
Retail book 27 times covered at EGP 5.30; a strong debut pulls money towards banks.
The number the central bank answers to; a rise above September keeps rates high.

views.call: Developers lag while rates stay high
views.note: From 26 Oct. Talaat Moustafa −1.5% since; the EGX30 +2.4%.

views.call: Dollar earners outperform as the pound slides
views.note: From 29 Oct. Orascom +0.9% and Elsewedy −0.7% on the day; judged over four weeks.

flows.title: Who bought and who sold
flows.sub: Net EGX equity flows, Thu 29 Oct, EGP bn
flows.read: Dominated by the execution of Banque du Caire's EGP 36.4 bn offering: foreign institutions bought, Egyptian institutions sold. Read normal days' flows, not this one, for who is backing the market.

global.finding: Alphabet's 12.6% fall on its results pulled the Nasdaq 1.4% lower; Walmart and JPMorgan rose as money moved to steadier names.

close.title: Thursday's close
close.note: A dash is a figure not yet confirmed by two sources this morning.

top.headline: Alphabet's AI-search miss hits big tech
top.body: Alphabet fell 12.6% after revenue missed and free cash flow turned negative, as AI Mode slowed search advertising. Amazon lost 4.3% and the Nasdaq 1.4%, while Walmart (+2.1%), JPMorgan (+1.3%) and Exxon (+0.7%) rose: money moved from AI spenders to steadier earnings.
top.view: Cautious on ad-funded and AI-heavy tech into Amazon's and Apple's results; the market is now asking for AI spending to pay back, not just to grow.
top.moves: Alphabet, Amazon and Broadcom most exposed; Walmart, JPMorgan and Berkshire as places money hides.
top.wrong: Alphabet recovers half its fall within a week, or the Nasdaq makes a new high before November's US inflation figure.
top.notice: Results dates for Apple and Amazon conflict between reports; check them before relying on the week ahead.

helped.name: Retail and staples: Walmart
helped.why: Up 2.1% on Thursday as money left tech; steady earnings are in demand while AI payback is questioned.

helped.name: Banks: JPMorgan
helped.why: Up 1.3%; higher-for-longer rates keep lending margins wide.

helped.name: Energy: Exxon Mobil
helped.why: Up 0.7% and 51% this year with Brent above $110; the oil price, not the day's news, drives it.

hurt.name: Search and ads: Alphabet
hurt.why: Down 12.6%: AI Mode is eating into search advertising faster than expected, and free cash flow turned negative.

hurt.name: Cloud spenders: Amazon
hurt.why: Down 4.3% in sympathy ahead of its own results; the same AI-spending question hangs over it.

hurt.name: AI chips: Broadcom, Nvidia
hurt.why: Down 1.9% and 0.8%; if the spenders slow, the chip makers' orders follow.

week.why: Sets the tone for rate bets and the dollar index, which feeds straight into the pound.
A hot reading pushes rate cuts further out and lifts the dollar.
The next test of whether AI spending pays back; reports disagree on the dates.

views.call: Money rotates from AI spenders to steady earners
views.note: From 29 Oct. Walmart +2.1% and JPMorgan +1.3% against Alphabet −12.6% on the day; judged over four weeks.

views.call: Alphabet's AI spend is priced in
views.note: Called on 27 Oct. Alphabet fell 12.6% on its results, so the view was wrong; it stays on the record.

egx.finding: The EGX30 rose 0.6% to 49,596 on Thursday, with the rate hike announced after the close; Alexandria Containers and Juhayna led your stocks, Abu Qir Fertilizers lagged.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: Thursday’s 100 bps hike raises what banks earn on loans and T-bills, which they hold in size, faster than it raises their deposit costs. CIB and EFG trade 8% and 6% below their 50-day averages, so little of this is priced in.

sectors.name: Investment banks and brokers
sectors.why: Banque du Caire’s retail tranche was 27 times covered and the state plans to list Enppi in January: more offerings mean more fees and more trading.

sectors.name: Dollar earners: contractors, cables, fertilisers
sectors.why: The dollar is 8% higher against the pound in a month, which lifts the pound value of export and overseas revenue at Orascom, Elsewedy and Abu Qir.

stocks.why: A return to its 50-day average (130.7). The hike widens margins, the stock is 16% below its 52-week high, and it trades near 5.5 times its last reported earnings.
stocks.wrong: it closes below EGP 114, 5% under Thursday’s close, or the EGX30 falls while it does.

stocks.why: Dollar revenue from Gulf and US projects gains from the weaker pound. Up 91% this year, so a pause is as likely as a new high.
stocks.wrong: it closes below EGP 780, 5% under Thursday, or the pound recovers sharply.

sectors.name: Real estate developers
sectors.why: Dearer financing hits instalment buyers and developers’ own borrowing at once. Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills are 12% and 16% below their 50-day averages and still falling, with both at their lowest since April.

sectors.name: Food and consumer
sectors.why: A weaker pound raises the cost of imported inputs such as milk powder and packaging; companies with pricing power, like Juhayna, pass it on with a lag.

stocks.why: Down 7.6% in a month and 12% under its 50-day average (91.3); the hike lands on its buyers and its debt. No sign yet of buyers stepping in.
stocks.wrong: it closes back above EGP 88, near its 50-day average, or a big sales launch beats expectations.

stocks.why: The same pressure as Talaat Moustafa with a smaller balance sheet: down 10.6% in a month and 16% under its 50-day average (13.5).
Profit-taking after a 73% run this year; it fell 3.5% on Thursday with no company news. The weaker pound helps its exports, so the downside should be limited.
stocks.wrong: it makes a new high above EGP 95.75.

egp.finding: The dollar is at EGP 56.04, near its 52-week high, after foreign investors sold local debt; Thursday's 100-basis-point hike is the central bank's answer.

drivers.name: Rates raised 100 bps
drivers.why: Deposit 20.00%, lending 21.00% on Thursday, the first rise since March 2024. Higher yields are meant to bring back the carry-trade money that left in October.

drivers.name: Foreign sales of local debt
drivers.why: Portfolio investors sold Egyptian treasuries as the dollar crossed 55 and then 56. Watch the next T-bill auction for whether demand returns.

drivers.name: IMF eighth and final review
drivers.why: The mission is in Cairo. A passed review releases the last tranche and steadies inflows; a delay would weigh on the pound.

drivers.name: Oil at $115
drivers.why: Brent near its 52-week high raises Egypt's fuel import bill, adding to dollar demand.

view.headline: The hike should cap the dollar near 56.5 for now
view.body: A 100-basis-point rise lifts T-bill yields back above inflation and pays foreign holders to stay. Most of the month's move was local, as the Pound or dollar chart shows.
view.moves: CIB and EFG Holding gain on wider margins and inflows; Talaat Moustafa and Palm Hills lose on dearer mortgages.
view.wrong: The dollar closes above EGP 57 before the next auction, or the auction's average yield falls rather than rises.

us.finding: Alphabet's 12.6% fall pulled the Nasdaq down 1.4%; the S&P 500 lost 0.3% and the Dow 0.3%, while Walmart and JPMorgan rose as money moved to steadier earnings.

afterBell.name: Amazon
afterBell.why: Earnings of $1.89 a share against $1.97 expected, revenue $201.9bn against $202.2bn.

afterBell.name: Intel
afterBell.why: Beat on adjusted earnings ($0.52 against $0.41) but missed on revenue at $16.5bn.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.why: Brent at $115, near its 52-week high, on Gulf shipping risk. Producers’ cash flow rises with every dollar on the barrel.

sectors.name: Banks
sectors.why: The 10-year Treasury near 5% and a December Fed hike in view widen lending margins; JPMorgan rose 1.3% on the day tech fell.

sectors.name: Steady earners
sectors.why: Money left AI spenders for predictable earnings on Thursday; Walmart is up 17% in a month. Rotations like this can reverse quickly.

stocks.why: At its 52-week high (184.54) and up 52% this year, carried by oil. More upside needs Brent to hold above $110.
stocks.wrong: Brent falls below $100, for example on a Gulf de-escalation.

stocks.why: Well above its 50-day average (109.8) after the rotation; its 52-week high of 134.20 is the ceiling to watch.
stocks.wrong: it closes below $115 as money returns to tech.

sectors.name: Big AI spenders
sectors.why: Alphabet fell 12.6% as AI search ate into its ad revenue, and Amazon dropped 6% after hours on a miss. Investors now want proof that AI spending pays.

sectors.name: Highly valued growth
sectors.why: A 10-year yield near 5% lowers what future profits are worth today, which weighs most on the most expensive stocks.

stocks.why: Missed on earnings ($1.89 against $1.97) and revenue, and fell about 6% after hours, which would take it near 229.
stocks.wrong: it closes back above $245 within two weeks of the results.

stocks.why: Already down 17.5% in a month and near its 52-week low (273.50), so much of the bad news is in the price; the risk is further downgrades.

global.finding: Brent held near $115 on Gulf shipping risk, gold slipped toward $4,000 as US yields stayed near 5%, and Bitcoin fell.

notes.brent: Egypt imports fuel, so a dearer barrel widens the import bill and adds to dollar demand; Gulf producers' cash, and their investment in Egypt, rises with it.
notes.gold_usd: Sets the base for Egyptian gold prices; Egyptians buy gold as a hedge against the pound, so local demand stays strong even as the world price falls.
notes.dxy: A stronger dollar pressures emerging-market currencies and pulls money out of their debt, Egypt's included.
notes.btc: A gauge of risk appetite; when it falls with tech stocks, investors are cutting risk, which rarely helps frontier markets.
